reading.title: Discussing a room concept
reading.text: At a room-planning workshop, Hana compares style descriptions rather than assumes every room has one label. Contemporary reflects current approaches, Traditional draws on established forms, and Scandinavian often emphasizes simple function and light. Industrial may expose structural or service elements. Bohemian mixes expressive materials and patterns. Mid-Century refers here to mid-twentieth-century design influences, while Farmhouse draws on rural domestic forms. Art Deco often uses geometric decoration. Japanese describes influences from Japanese design traditions, and Coastal evokes a seaside setting. Hana prepares a color palette before selecting an accent wall. Wallpaper is a wall covering, paint is a coating, and tile is a hard modular finish. She explains how the choices address the brief without turning cultural labels into fixed rules about people's homes.

reading.title: Comparing finishes and light
reading.text: Hana compares floor samples before selecting lighting. Hardwood is timber flooring; carpet is a textile covering. Stone is a wider material category, while marble is one kind of stone. Concrete is a separate building material. A chandelier has several light sources, and a pendant light hangs from above. Track lighting supports lights along a track. A recessed light sits within the ceiling. A floor lamp stands on the floor, whereas a table lamp sits on furniture. A sconce is fixed to a wall. Natural light comes from daylight; a dimmer changes the light output of a suitable lamp. An LED strip is a flexible line of small light-emitting devices. Hana checks compatibility and the room's needs rather than infers electrical safety from a photograph.

reading.title: Selecting room accessories
reading.text: Hana prepares a small accessory board. An area rug covers part of the floor; curtains hang at the window, and a throw pillow adds a small cushion to a seat. Artwork may be a drawing, painting or another creative piece. A mirror reflects the room, whereas a vase holds flowers or serves as decoration. A candle is a wax object with a wick, and a plant is a living organism that may need care. A sculpture has three-dimensional form, while a photo frame surrounds a photograph. Hana asks whether each item has a practical purpose, a decorative purpose, or both. She leaves routes clear in the proposed layout. The board supports a conversation about choices rather than proves that a room meets an accessibility standard.
